cita: Hu et al. (2026). EvoRepair: Enhancing Vulnerability Repair Agents Through Experience-Based Self-Evolution.
problema: LLM-based automated vulnerability repair (AVR) agents lack intra-vulnerability experience accumulation (they repeat mistakes across repair trajectories for the same CVE) and cross-vulnerability experience reuse (each CVE is repaired in isolation despite shared CWE/CVE taxonomies suggesting transferable repair patterns).
mecanismo: Cyclic learn-and-repair loop: after each repair turn the agent reflects on its trajectory and constructs a structured 5-dimension experience entry (vuln description, repair strategy, trajectory analysis, actionable rules, reflection), which an LLM-as-Judge scores for quality+generalizability before admission and which is compressed to bound growth; retrieval before each turn is a two-stage rerank (top-M by similarity, then top-K by a blended similarity+score) that always includes the target CVE's own history plus other CVEs matched by CWE/CVE similarity.
evaluacion: 12 representative AVR baselines on PATCHEVAL and SEC-bench using GPT-5-mini, plus cross-model/cross-language/cross-dataset transfer experiments on VUL4J; ablates the two warm-up strategies (Standard Patch vs Pre-repair) and the turn-level early-stopping rule.
numeros_clave: 93.47% PATCHEVAL, 87.00% SEC-bench, 90.46% overall; beats LoopRepair by 39.56%/33.50%, IntentFix by 70.86%/50.50%, and Live-SWE-Agent by 6.98% overall (Abstract).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: The LLM-as-Judge quality+generalizability scoring gate before an experience enters the bank (Sec 3.3.3) is a concrete pattern MF could adopt for promoting transient gotchas to durable recipes.
The turn-level yield-rate alpha = growth(repair)/growth(cost) early-stopping rule (Sec 3.3.2, Eq.4) operationalizes bounding spend when marginal returns fall, matching MF's context-economy concern.

The 'Understand Vulnerability' skill explicitly outputs a hypothesis and checklist before repair begins (Table 2), i.e. a plan-state artifact carried turn over turn -- a pattern MF's PLAN-ESTADO could formalize.
Retrieval is explicitly measured via a two-stage similarity+score rerank (Sec 3.3.1, Eq.1-3) rather than assumed, aligning with MF's G-M2 need for a measured retrieval layer.

notes: Numbers from Abstract + Sec 3.3.1 (retrieval scoring Eq.1-3, read at 30k-char budget). Plan_estado=SI justified by the checklist/hypothesis output of the Understand-Vulnerability skill (Table 2).

cita: Xu, J., Szlam, A. y Weston, J. (2022). Beyond Goldfish Memory: Long-Term Open-Domain Conversation.
problema: State-of-the-art open-domain dialogue models are trained/evaluated on short single-session conversations (2-15 turns) with token-truncation lengths as low as 128, so they cannot recall or build on information from earlier sessions with the same user -- a 'goldfish memory' limitation.
mecanismo: After each chat session a human/model summarizer distills salient personal points into a session summary (WRITE); the next session's model chooses between raw dialogue history vs the generated summary as long-term memory (ADMISION), and later a supervised encoder-decoder is trained to predict summaries at inference (CONSOLIDACION); retrieval is hybrid -- either the concatenated summaries as extended context, or retrieval-augmentation (RAG/FiD/FiD-RAG with a DPR bi-encoder) over session-level documents to select the most relevant past sessions.
evaluacion: Releases the Multi-Session Chat (MSC) dataset (5 sessions, human-human crowdworker chats) and compares BST 2.7B token-truncation baselines vs retrieval-augmented (RAG/FiD/FiD-RAG) vs summarization-memory models via validation/test perplexity across sessions 2-5 and session-openings specifically.
numeros_clave: SumMem-MSC (FiD-RAG) test perplexity 7.87 vs BST 2.7B baseline 12.92 on session openings (Table 7); gold-summary context improves perplexity by ~2 points over no-context on openings (Table 4).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: Summarizing sessions into salient points before storing them (Sec 4.3) is exactly the gotcha-to-recipe consolidation MF targets, and it measurably beats storing raw history (Table 3/7).
Retrieval quality is measured directly via perplexity deltas across retrieval strategies (Table 3/7), supporting MF's insistence on a MEASURED retrieval layer rather than an assumed one.
Summaries reduce truncation (fewer tokens truncated, last column of Table 3) while matching or beating full dialogue history -- a token-economy pattern MF's Tier-1 narrative could reuse.

notes: Numbers from Table 3/4/7 (perplexity by session and context type). Founding MSC-dataset paper; plan_estado=NO.

cita: Zhang et al. (2022). History-Aware Hierarchical Transformer for Multi-session Open-domain Dialogue System.
problema: Existing multi-session dialogue models either truncate history (losing long-term context) or need to retrieve a very large portion of raw conversation text to beat a plain Transformer, so incorporating history is still bounded by short token-truncation lengths and costly retrieval.
mecanismo: History conversations are hierarchically encoded per-utterance (Transformer encoder + max-pooling) and aggregated by a self-attentive mechanism into a condensed history memory vector per session (WRITE); a history-aware context encoder attends between this memory matrix and the current turn and UPDATES it (ACTUALIZACION); a history-aware decoder switches between generating from a generic vocabulary and copying tokens directly from history (CopyNet-style) -- a dense VECTOR representation, not explicit top-k text search.
evaluacion: Facebook MSC dataset (sessions 2-5); automatic metrics BLEU-2/3 and ROUGE-L against BlenderBot/BlenderBotmsc/FiD-RAG baselines, plus human evaluation (readability/context/history relevancy, Fleiss' Kappa) and an ablation removing hierarchical encoding, the history encoder, and the switching mechanism.
numeros_clave: HAHT session-5 R-L 16.42 vs BlenderBotmsc 16.10 (Table 2); on session-opening data HAHT beats FiD-RAG/BlenderBotmsc by 10.6%/9.1% BLEU-3 at session 4 (Table 4); ablation shows removing the history encoder causes the largest drop across all metrics (Table 5).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: The history memory matrix, continuously updated per turn (Sec 3.2), is a compact DERIVED index over raw conversation -- a concrete instance of a Tier-3 cache MF could model for its own derived index.
The ablation study (Table 5) directly measures the marginal contribution of each memory component (hierarchy, history-encoder, switch), reinforcing MF's measured-retrieval requirement.
Dense hierarchical encoding avoids concatenating full raw history, a token-cost concern, but the paper reports only quality metrics, not latency/token counts (Sec 5.4).

notes: Numbers in Table 2 (automatic eval), Table 4 (session openings), Table 5 (ablation). plan_estado=NO.

cita: Packer et al. (2023). MemGPT: Towards LLMs as Operating Systems.
problema: LLMs have fixed, limited context windows that prevent long conversations and analysis of documents/histories exceeding that window, and naive truncation or blind summarization loses information needed for consistency and engagement.
mecanismo: OS-inspired virtual context management: main context (system instructions + working context + FIFO queue) holds only in-context data; when the FIFO queue nears capacity a queue manager emits a 'memory pressure' system alert so the LLM can self-direct WRITEs to working context (structured facts) or archival/recall storage (unbounded external DB, pgvector); old messages are evicted from the FIFO queue, recursively summarized, and moved to recall storage (OLVIDO/ACTUALIZACION, like OS disk paging); retrieval is function-call driven -- the LLM issues explicit paginated search queries against archival/recall storage and decides when to page data back into context.
evaluacion: Deep memory retrieval (DMR, consistency) and conversation-opener (engagement) tasks on an extended MSC dataset; document QA and nested key-value retrieval tasks over documents/Wikipedia articles far exceeding context length; compares GPT-3.5/GPT-4/GPT-4-Turbo with and without MemGPT.
numeros_clave: DMR accuracy: GPT-3.5 38.7%->66.9%, GPT-4 32.1%->92.5%, GPT-4 Turbo 35.3%->93.4% with MemGPT (Table 2); document QA accuracy stays flat as retrieved-document count grows (Figure 5) unlike fixed-context baselines that degrade.

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: The 'memory pressure' system alert that triggers self-directed writes to working/archival storage (Sec 2.2) is a concrete discretionary write-trigger mechanism directly relevant to MF's G-M1.
Working context (small, curated) vs archival/recall storage (unbounded) mirrors a Tier-1/derived-cache split MF could model directly (Sec 2.1).
Retrieval is entirely function-call driven and paginated, letting the agent measure/decide what to bring back into context (Sec 2.3), matching MF's measured-retrieval stance over blind concatenation.

notes: Numbers Table 2 (DMR) + Figure 5 (doc QA). plan_estado=NO; canonical OS-memory paper, high MF relevance.

cita: Liu et al. (2023). Think-in-Memory: Recalling and Post-thinking Enable LLMs with Long-Term Memory.
problema: Memory-augmented LLMs that store and re-reason over raw historical dialogue text produce inconsistent reasoning across turns (different reasoning paths for the same recalled history) and incur costly pairwise-similarity retrieval over the whole memory as conversations grow.
mecanismo: After generating a response the LLM 'post-thinks', extracting inductive thoughts (relation triples) and inserting them -- not raw text -- into a hash-indexed memory cache (WRITE); explicit insert/forget/merge operations keep the cache free of contradictory or duplicate thoughts (CONSOLIDACION/OLVIDO); retrieval is two-stage -- locality-sensitive hashing (LSH) narrows to a nearby bucket, then similarity search within that bucket recalls top-k thoughts, avoiding both repeated reasoning over raw history and whole-memory pairwise comparison (HIBRIDA: text thoughts + hash/LSH index).
evaluacion: KdConv (Chinese knowledge-driven dialogue), a Generated Virtual Dataset (GVD, 15 virtual ChatGPT users over 10 days), and a real-world medical dataset (RMD, 1800 conversations); baselines = no-memory and SiliconFriend (raw-text memory); ChatGLM and Baichuan2 backbones with LoRA fine-tuning; a dedicated retrieval-time benchmark and a top-k recall accuracy sweep.
numeros_clave: Retrieval time: baseline (pairwise over whole memory) 0.6287ms vs TiM (LSH-narrowed) 0.5305ms, about 0.1ms faster (Table 3); top-10 recall achieves 0.973 retrieval accuracy on KdConv-Travel (Sec 4.3.2).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: The explicit insert/forget/merge trio over stored 'thoughts' (Sec 3.4, Table 1) is a directly reusable consolidation-operation vocabulary MF could adopt for promoting gotchas to recipes.
TiM measures and reports a concrete retrieval-latency reduction from bucket-narrowed (LSH) search vs whole-memory pairwise comparison (Table 3), supporting MF's cost/latency lens on retrieval design.
The 'Forget' operation explicitly removes counterfactual/contradictory thoughts (Fig.4) -- a concrete anti-drift mechanism relevant to MF's FIDELIDAD anchor (poisoning/staleness).

notes: Numbers Table 3 (retrieval time) + Sec 4.3.2 (top-k recall). plan_estado=NO.

cita: Ong et al. (2024). Towards Lifelong Dialogue Agents via Timeline-based Memory Management.
problema: Conventional memory-update strategies (updating/replacing/deleting old memories to keep retrieval quality high) can silently discard important early context (e.g. a persona fact learned once), causing biased or contradictory responses that ignore relevant past events.
mecanismo: New session memories (event, time) are summarized and linked into a directed memory graph using LLM-assigned temporal + cause-effect commonsense relations (Cause/Reason/Want/...), explicitly never deleting old nodes (WRITE, no OLVIDO); retrieval finds top-k memories then extracts/untangles whole 'timelines' -- linear chains from the connected component -- rather than isolated facts, and an LLM refines the raw timeline against the current dialogue context before it augments response generation (CONSOLIDACION).
evaluacion: Automatic metrics (BLEU-4, ROUGE-L, MAUVE, BERTScore) on Multi-Session Chat and Conversation Chronicles vs memory-retrieval/memory-update/RSum-LLM/MemoChat/COMEDY baselines; G-Eval and human head-to-head evaluation of retrieval helpfulness; a novel counterfactual-driven 'TeaFarm' evaluation pipeline; ablations removing relation-aware linking, timeline refinement, and timeline order (shuffled).
numeros_clave: THEANINE MAUVE 64.41 vs best baseline 38.16 (Memory Retrieval) on Conversation Chronicles (Table 1); human-judged golden-memory retrieval accuracy 72% vs Memory Retrieval 68% / +Memory Update 64% (Table 3); ablation ranking: relation-aware linking > timeline-as-whole > timeline refinement (Table 2).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: THEANINE builds a persistent memory graph, never deleting old memories, and consolidates via retrieved 'timelines' rather than single facts (Sec 2.1-2.2) -- a concrete pattern MF could adopt for turning gotchas into durable linked structure.

Empirically, conventional memory-UPDATE (deleting/replacing old memories to keep retrieval clean) HURTS response quality vs never deleting (Table 1, Finding 1) -- this challenges any assumption that pruning stale facts is safe by default; staleness should be re-contextualized, not deleted.
Ablations (Table 2) and human-judged retrieval accuracy (Table 3) directly measure which retrieval design choices matter, in line with MF's measured-retrieval principle.

notes: Numbers Table 1 (automatic eval), Table 2 (ablation), Table 3 (human-judged retrieval accuracy). plan_estado=NO.
